title: Fixed on with plural owners
summary: Use fixed on with meillä, teillä, and heillä to say what the owner has.
objectives: Use fixed on with meillä, teillä, and heillä to say what the owner has.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Use fixed on with meillä, teillä, and heillä to say what the owner has.
Meillä on pallo means “We have a ball”. Keep on even though meillä names several owners; olemme belongs to “We are …”.
keyPoints: Use fixed on with meillä, teillä, and heillä to say what the owner has.

steps: Meillä names several owners, but the possession verb stays on, not olemme.
pallo (“ball”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Teillä addresses a group here; use on, not olette.
kynä (“pen”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
Heillä names several owners; use on, not ovat.
peli (“game”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
A front-vowel noun such as tyyny changes neither the owners nor fixed on.
tyyny (“pillow”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.

commonMistakes: Possession uses on with every owner: meillä on, not meillä olemme; heillä on, not heillä ovat.
Several owners can have one thing. A plural owner does not turn pallo into a plural noun.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Write “They have a ball.” in Finnish. Use heillä (“they as the owner”) and pallo (“a ball”). Frame: “Heillä ___ pallo”.
practiceExercises.explanation: Possession uses on with every owner. Plural owners still take on; ovat belongs to a different sentence pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.
pallo stays in its basic singular form: one ball.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed on in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
